newsitem.title: CANADA: Falling golds not seen halting Toronto stock rally.
newsitem.headline: Falling golds not seen halting Toronto stock rally.

text.p: The decline in key gold stocks will not derail the recent rally on the Toronto Stock Exchange, analysts said on Monday, citing momentum in financial issues and other sectors of Canada's largest equities market.
Douglas Davis, president of money management group Davis-Rea Ltd Investment Counsel, saw Toronto's rally persisting since golds were traditionally the last group to climb.
Rising sectors such as financial services were poised for further gains, buoyed by low interest rates, he said.

"There is momentum (among non-gold stocks) and because their momentum is continuing to be encouraged by the low rates, the stock market will continue to carry on until such time as the rates go up," Davis said, predicting more record highs in July and August.

Dropping bullion prices slashed 4.1 percent on Monday from the key gold group, which makes up 8.4 percent of Toronto's 300 Composite Index. The key index of Canada's biggest equities exchange shed 56 points to close at 6529 on Monday, after posting a record high 6615 last Thursday.

The closely watched Comex price in New York shed $6.20 to 319.00 on Monday after Australia's central bank disclosed last week that it sold off over 60 percent of its gold reserves, capping recent sales by several European central banks.
Analysts estimated that the new possible lows for bullion prices ranged from $275 to $298.
The gold price fell below $314 an ounce on Monday, but stabilized overnight to around S319.

Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram said the heavy turnover in shares of Canada's two largest gold miners was a possible signal that gold bullion, now at 12-year lows, may not have much further to drop.
"There's very big volume on Barrick (Gold Corp ) and Placer Dome (Inc ) and sometimes you get the big volume as you're approaching some kind of bottoming process," he said.
Placer topped Toronto actives on Monday, shedding 1.20 to 19.25 on 5.3 million shares. Barrick was second most active, off 0.40 to 27.80 on 4.8 million shares.

But John Ing, president of brokerage Maison Placements Canada, was more bearish on the outlook for Toronto's market as bullion prices continued to dive. "These golds stocks are going to follow bullion and (are) heading lower."
